questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Grime music and the places it came from
How to design better tower blocks in London
Why pirate radio stations were closed down
The life story of the singer Stormzy
questions.why: Neil says they're talking about grime, a style of music which originated in London's tower blocks.

questions.q: How does Sam describe her taste in music?
options: She only listens to grime
She doesn't really like music
She likes many different styles
She prefers classical music
questions.why: Sam says she doesn't have one specific type – her taste is 'eclectic', including a wide variety of styles.

options: In music schools in central London
In tower blocks in east and southeast London
In nightclubs in American cities
In recording studios owned by the BBC
questions.why: Neil says it originated in the tower blocks of east and southeast London.

questions.q: What does Jude Yawson say happened on his estate when he was about seven or eight?
options: His family moved to a different part of London
The old tower blocks were knocked down
He started making music with his friends
Life there became more tense, with more conflict
questions.why: He says things 'started to get a bit more contentious' as new people moved in and police harassed people.

questions.q: How does Jude now feel about his teacher's advice about stabbing?
options: He thinks it was a joke at the time
He still thinks it was completely normal
He wonders why a teenager needed to hear it
He is angry that the teacher said nothing
questions.why: He felt grateful at 14, but in hindsight questions why a teenager should receive that information.

questions.q: How did grime music first spread?
options: Through pirate radio stations
Through big concerts in stadiums
Through TV talent shows
Through music videos in cinemas
questions.why: Neil says it started in bedrooms and basements, with many artists' works broadcast on pirate radio.

questions.q: What do some critics think of grime music?
options: It is too slow and quiet to enjoy
It copies American music too closely
It is only popular with older people
Its lyrics and beats make violence seem good
questions.why: Sam says some think the hard-hitting lyrics and strong beats glorify violence.

questions.q: How does Jude Yawson see grime differently from its critics?
options: As an angry and violent kind of music
As a 'soulful shout' people need to let out
As music written mainly for young children
As a simple copy of Wiley's early songs
questions.why: He describes grime as 'a soulful shout… there's a necessity in literally getting all of this content out'.
